description: Hey! We're a small beginner-friendly team developing Analog Catalog, a web app exploring places on Earth with similar environment and geology to Mars and the Moon. Our team has a background in C#, graphic design, planetary sciences and communication. We're looking for folks interested in geology, programming, and data analysis to help us grow. We're beginners ourselves, no experience required, just to be willing to learn & collaborate.

details:
Hidden Analogs is an interactive 3D map showing eight lesser known places on Earth that bear a resemblance to the Moon or Mars. Instead of focusing on well-known sites such as Devon Island or Utah, we looked for places with published evidence that have received little attention: a Saharan volcano compared with Elysium Mons, an acidic spring deposit in Canada's Arctic, a hyperarid desert in Peru, a basalt impact crater in India, a lava tube in Saudi Arabia, a fresh rayed crater in Egypt, an anorthosite massif in Madagascar, and an acid salt lake in Western Australia. We deliberately excluded famous analog sites. Instead we chose locations with published evidence, compared each with a specific place on the Moon or Mars, and weighed practical factors like how remote it is, accessability, and if it may have protected or heritage status. The aim of our project is to demonstrate how open space agency data can let scientists look beyond well-known sites and make consistent comparisons between places they tend to overlook.

Every marker follows the same format: measurements of the site from papers we read, a Moon or Mars comparison using NASA’s Moon Trek and Mars Trek and LRO imagery, a short explanation of what the place could teach us, and a list of its limits. Sources are listed on our Data and Sources page. The map was built with MapTiler’s mapping library, and C#, using NASA ASTER & AppEEARS 3D terrain. Our research came from papers reviewed by peers and NASA and space agency reports. The map gives people who are interested in the field of analogs a quick way to find out about over looked analog sites and see what each one can and can’t teach us, and because every card lists the site's limits, it shows no analog is a perfect match. We could make it grow by adding more sites.
